subject: WestUS4: phased node reset & driver refresh — customer notices + post-run checklist
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@stratoscloud.com>, infra-ops@stratoscloud.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: WestUS4: phased node reset & driver refresh — customer notices + post-run checklist

Hi Sofia / Stratos infra team,

We wanted to give you an early heads-up about a planned, phased maintenance window in the WestUS4 region next Wednesday (2026-10-21) to roll a kernel + GPU driver refresh across a subset of inferencing nodes. This is a rolling, capacity-aware update designed to keep latency SLOs intact for high-priority tenants; however, some customers with pinned capacity may experience short (~10–60s) connections resets during the node restart for KV cache warming.

Key details (summary):
- Window: 2026-10-21 03:00–08:00 UTC (phased across AZs, targeting minimal overlapping customer shards)
- Scope: kernel 6.4.x -> 6.5.x backported security and NVIDIA driver 545.x -> 555.x for driver stability.
- Impact: short-lived reconnects; we will attempt single-node drains and live migration where supported. No model data migration expected.
- Customers affected: customers with dedicated pools in WestUS4, and a small subset of hosted requests routed to dedicated pools.

What we will do for StratosCloud:
1) Provide a pre-window notice to your SRE and procurement contacts 48 hours in advance (this email serves as the 72-hour notice).
2) Provide a targeted runbook and a post-run checklist.
3) Assign an on-call run coordinator and a postmortem owner to investigate any regressions.

I've attached the phased playbook (westus4_phased_playbook_v1.pdf) and included our internal runbook link. Please let me know if you have blackout constraints or if you'd like us to run on a different date.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Ops Manager — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

We have a major billing cutover scheduled on 2026-10-21 07:30–08:30 UTC which overlaps the tail of your window. Can you confirm that nodes serving StratosCloud will not be in a restart during that exact minute? If necessary we can accept a slightly earlier or later slot for our pinned pools.

Also please add our SRE lead (infra-ops@stratoscloud.com) to the notification cadence and include the run coordinator details when assigned.

—Sofia

Hi Sofia — thanks for flagging the billing cutover window. We can accommodate a hard exclusion for StratosCloud’s pinned pools between 07:20–08:40 UTC (we'll schedule your pool to be updated either earlier in the window or after 08:45). I’ll set that in the orchestration policy and mark your pools as blackout-protected.

Run coordinator: Hannah Schmitt (hannah_schmitt@redwood.com) — she'll be the primary on-call during the window. Monica will be the customer comms point for escalation. Rishi will own KPIs and telemetry checks post-run.

I've attached a short pre-flight checklist and the phased playbook in the shared drive link. Please confirm you want the exclusion applied to all StratosCloud pinned pools in WestUS4.

Aditya

Subject: Re: WestUS4: phased node reset & driver refresh — customer notices + post-run checklist

Confirmed — please apply the blackout to all pinned pools for StratosCloud in WestUS4. We'll also standby for an on-call bridge invite 15 minutes before your window.

One question: will there be any driver-level tuning that requires model re-quantization or is the update purely compatibility/stability-focused? We have a small number of optimizations tied to 545.x behavior.

—Ops

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@stratoscloud.com>, infra-ops@stratoscloud.com, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-run plan & postmortem template (WestUS4 maintenance)

Forwarding the final run plan and our postmortem template. After the window completes we'll run the KPIs in this order: 1) 99th/50th pct latency for pinned pools, 2) error-rate by model, 3) KV cache miss rate and rippling cost delta, 4) reconnection incidence per customer. If any threshold exceeds the runaway criteria in the playbook we will roll back the driver on the affected node set and escalate.

Quick answers: the driver update is compatibility/stability-focused. We do not expect forced re-quantization, but Rishi will run a limited sample run for your optimizations in the minutes after the update to validate output parity. If any model-specific divergence appears we'll capture diffs and surface with concrete remediation steps.

Bridge: link will be posted to the drive doc 15 minutes before window. Postmortem owner: Markus Klein (markus_klein@redwood.com). Attachment: postmortem-template.docx

—Hannah
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
